validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed by an independent, detailed, on-point source that is NOT the EGAS AR2018 map already cited. A youm7.com article (2013-07-19, already the sheet's own Start [ref]/ProjectLevelCost [ref]) quotes EGAS Holding Vice-Chairman Khaled Abdel Badie by name saying operational trials had just finished on 'khat el-Sadat-Dahshour' ('the Sadat-Dahshour line'), diameter 42 inches, length 75 km, built by Petrojet and supervised by GASCO, at an investment cost of 600 million EGP borne by EGAS, whose purpose is to raise gas pressure in the Kuraimat area feeding the Kuraimat combined-cycle power station that serves Greater Cairo. I fetched the full article body (not just the substring the automated checker probed) and confirm 'al-Sadat-Dahshour' appears verbatim as the line's own name, not as an artifact of an unrelated headline (the headline itself is about the Kuraimat power-station tie-in, which had raised my suspicion this ref might actually belong to a Kuraimat-family row like P8014/P8021 -- it does not; the body is explicitly and solely about this Sadat-Dahshour line, and Kuraimat is named only as the DOWNSTREAM consumer it feeds, consistent with GEM's own EndPrefecture=Dahshour, not Kuraimat).

SECOND TEST APPLIED, per this cohort's known map-citation pattern: I fetched the EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF cited on Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location, ran pdftotext -layout (no hit on 'Sadat' or the exact segment -- expected, since that text layer is only the LIST of pipelines newly completed IN FY2017/2018, and this line was built in 2013), then rendered the actual GASCO national-grid MAP graphic on the report's printed p.35 (PDF page 19) at 400dpi and visually read it, per this cohort's rule that a text-search miss on this report is not evidence against a map-sourced row. The map shows a callout at 'El Sadat' reading 'Natgas 6 October / 42" 74 km' on the same west-of-Cairo corridor GEM records (Sadat/Monufia -> Dahshour/Giza runs via 6th of October City, which sits on that route). The map's own printed length is 74 km -- an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=74.00, and the diameter (42") is an exact match too. The map labels the corridor by an intermediate waypoint ('6 October') rather than by GEM's chosen endpoint ('Dahshour'); I read this as the same physical corridor identified by two different landmarks along its route, not a contradiction -- 6th of October City and Dahshur are both on the west-bank Giza corridor between Sadat and the Kuraimat feed, and nothing on the map or in the article suggests two distinct 42in/74-75km lines exist in this corridor.

CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded gas transmission trunk (42in trunk diameter, part of the GASCO 'National Gas Grid', consistent with PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas).

DUPLICATE check against the 40-row roster: not a duplicate. Distinct specs from every other Kuraimat/Dahshour/Ameriya-area row in the watchlist -- P8014 Zaafarana-Kuraimat (18in/163km) and P8021 Kuraimat-Al Tebbin (22in/87km) are separate, smaller-diameter downstream feeds to the same Kuraimat power station, not the same physical pipe as this 42in/74km trunk; P8032 Ameriya-Dahshour (32in/200km) differs in both diameter and length. No same-name/same-spec collision found.

ATTRIBUTION: StartState/Province=Monufia is correct for Sadat City (Al-Sadat City is administratively in Monufia Governorate); EndState/Province=Giza is correct for Dahshur (the Dahshur necropolis/area sits in Giza Governorate on the west bank south of Cairo). Both check out geographically.

SPEC: Length -- GEM 74.00 km vs. map 74 km (exact) vs. youm7's rounded 75 km (a spoken-interview approximation) -- immaterial, not a material disagreement. Diameter -- GEM 42in matches both sources exactly. ProjectLevelCost -- GEM 600,000,000 EGP matches youm7's '600 million EGP' (i.e. 600 مليون جنيه) exactly; the automated existing_ref_checks flagged this as unmatched only because it searched for a literal digit string ('600000000') against a source that states the figure in words -- I read the full article and confirm the value is correct, this is a false-alarm from the substring checker, not a real discrepancy. StartYear1=2013 matches the article's own dateline and 'trials just completed' framing.

Status=operating: consistent -- trials/construction finished per the 2013 article, no indication anywhere of a later shutdown.

Overall this is one of the better-sourced rows in this batch: it already carries two genuinely independent, on-point, verified sources (map + press interview) across its ref cells, it just wasn't cross-linked -- Length/Diameter/Location/Status/Fuel/PipelineType cite only the map today even though youm7 independently corroborates Length, Diameter, and the Sadat/Dahshour naming.

summary: P8039 confirmed (caveat), concern_type=none: real, correctly named/classified 42in/74km Sadat-Dahshour transmission trunk, independently corroborated by a 2013 youm7 EGAS-official interview (exact diameter/cost match, Kuraimat downstream purpose named explicitly) plus visual read of the EGAS AR2018 GASCO national-grid map (exact 42in/74km label on the same corridor); no existence, duplicate, classification, attribution, or material spec issues found.
